title: Personal care, accessible communication and withdrawn consent

communication_needs: Needs the speaker to face him and reduce background noise
Do not assume agreement when he has not heard a question
explicit_preferences: Prefers to wash his face and upper body independently
Wants the door closed before personal care
patient.dialogue_style: Direct and friendly when he can hear; becomes quiet if rushed
nonverbal_palette: Mr Chen tilts his better ear towards the learner and watches their face closely.
He reaches for the washcloth before answering.
His shoulders tense and he raises one hand slightly.

outcomes: Establish preferences and obtain consent before personal care
Support independence rather than taking over
Recognise and respond immediately when consent is withdrawn

prebrief.role: You are the student nurse supporting Mr Chen with morning personal care on the rehabilitation ward.
prebrief.orientation: Make communication accessible, establish what help is wanted and respond to consent as an ongoing process.
resources: Privacy controls represented in text and nursing notes
limitations: No physical personal-care procedure is performed
The app represents consent and environment through authored state
AI cannot infer capacity, new impairment or a care procedure
ground_rules: Describe only assistance you would provide with permission
Hearing access must not be treated as a measure of cognition
The encounter may be paused and is followed by facilitated debrief

clinical.presenting_context: Requires some assistance with lower-body washing after reduced mobility
visible_at_start: Television is on and the door is open
Mr Chen has a washcloth within reach
clinical.allergy_record: Not relevant to this personal-care scenario

clinical_workspace.handover: Mr Chen is regaining mobility and needs some lower-body assistance. He usually manages his face and upper body independently and uses hearing aids.
environment: Washcloth and toiletries are within reach
available_resources: Private care space represented in text

time_events.visible_cue: Mr Chen raises his hand and says, 'Stop a moment, please.'

allowed_actions.label: Reduce background noise and face Mr Chen
Ask whether Mr Chen wants help checking his hearing aid
reveals: Mr Chen accepts help reseating the loose hearing aid

allowed_actions.label: Close the door and prepare the private care space
Ask what Mr Chen wants to do independently
reveals: Mr Chen wants to wash his face and upper body himself
allowed_actions.blocked_message: First make it easier for Mr Chen to hear the question.

allowed_actions.label: Explain the proposed assistance and seek consent
reveals: Mr Chen agrees to limited assistance with lower-body care
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Privacy and Mr Chen's preferences should be established first.

allowed_actions.label: Begin only the assistance Mr Chen agreed to
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Valid consent has not been established.

allowed_actions.label: Stop care immediately and ask what Mr Chen needs
reveals: Mr Chen says the water feels too cold and wants a pause
allowed_actions.blocked_message: This action becomes relevant only if consent is withdrawn.

must_not_generate: Judgement or grading of the student

facilitator_only.opening_brief: The learner is asked to support Mr Chen with morning personal care.
expected_safety_points: Hearing needs shape access, not cognition
The patient controls how much assistance is provided
Withdrawal of consent leads to an immediate pause
pause_triggers: Learner continues personal care after the withdrawal cue

educator_rubric.label: Accessible communication
educator_rubric.guidance: Reduces avoidable noise, faces Mr Chen and checks hearing support without making cognitive assumptions.

educator_rubric.label: Choice and independence
educator_rubric.guidance: Asks what Mr Chen wants to do himself and limits assistance to what he requests.

educator_rubric.label: Privacy and ongoing consent
educator_rubric.guidance: Creates privacy, explains the proposed help and treats consent as revisable throughout.

educator_rubric.label: Response to withdrawal
educator_rubric.guidance: Stops immediately when asked and explores what Mr Chen needs before any further care.

prompts: Which environmental change most improved communication?
How did you preserve independence during care?
What should happen after consent is withdrawn?

dialogue.opening_line: Sorry, I didn't catch that—the television is quite loud.

action_responses.reduce_noise: That's much better. I can hear you when you face me like that.
action_responses.check_hearing_support: Yes please—the left hearing aid feels loose.
action_responses.create_privacy: Thank you for closing the door.
action_responses.check_preferences: I can wash my face and upper body myself. I only need help lower down.
action_responses.seek_consent: Yes, I agree to that amount of help.
action_responses.start_agreed_care: All right, I'm ready to begin.
action_responses.pause_on_withdrawal: Thank you for stopping. The water feels too cold; I need a moment.

fallback_responses: Please face me when you speak so I can follow you.
Mr Chen waits for the background noise to settle before replying.

facts.fact: He wants to wash his face and upper body independently and needs help only with lower-body washing.
He can hear more clearly when the speaker faces him and the background noise is reduced.
He has withdrawn consent because the water feels too cold and wants care to pause.

check_preferences: ask what he wants to do
